thread:
alex: heads up — after last runtime deploy we saw prefix cache hit-rate drop from ~92% -> ~64% on prod for chat flows using the system prompt. noticed latency climb on p50 too. anyone else seeing this?

rina: saw it in dashboards, yes. spike started right after the tokenizer bump in the deploy.

sam: confirm — tokenizer version changed from 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 in the image. small tokenization diffs can change cache keys a lot.

alex: my hypothesis: we compute cache key as sha256(tokenizer(encoded prompt) + model + system_prompt_hash + tools_signature). tokenizer change altered tokens -> miss.

mike: +1. also found some callers started including the tool fields even when empty, which changes the serialized key.

jonathan: quick numbers from hit-rate drilldown: overall requests 1.2M last hour, expected hits 1.1M at old 92% hit-rate, actual hits 768k. ~332k extra cold token generation. cost delta obvious.

alex: profiling snapshot after repro: kernel selection unchanged, but tokenization time moved from 8% -> 11% of request CPU, and KV lookup still tiny time but misses cause big perf for long prefixes.

rina: can we add token-level normalization into the key rather than raw string? e.g., always use tokenizer.version + token ids sequence. that would surface tokenizer mismatch though.

sam: we should pin tokenizer version into the cache key explicitly. if tokenizer changes, hits go to zero until we migrate. better than silent drift.

mike: proposed action list:
- normalize prompt whitespace and unicode NFKC before tokenizing
- canonicalize tool/function call fields (sort keys, omit empty arrays)
- include tokenizer_version in cache_key_v meta
- add metric cache_key_hash_v so we can count key-space churn

alex: example canonicalization snippet (pseudo):
```
def canonicalize_request(req):
  req.system = nkfc_normalize(req.system).strip()
  req.prompt = collapse_whitespace(req.prompt)
  req.tools = sort_keys(remove_empty(req.tools))
  return f\"v2|tk:{TOKENIZER_VER}|m:{req.model}|sys:{sha1(req.system)}|p:{sha1(req.prompt)}|tools:{sha1(json_dump(req.tools))}\"
```

jonathan: we need to be careful with including tokenizer ver directly in key if we want cross-version hits during controlled rollouts. maybe support dual-key lookups for N hours: look for key with current tokenizer ver, then fallback to previous pinned ver for a grace period.

rina: fallback is nice but costly to implement. alternative: pre-warm cache after tokenizer deploy — run synthetic warmup using top prefixes. That buys time while hits rebuild.

sam: warmup plan: extract top 5k prefixes from analytics, generate warmup traffic to dedicated warmup pool that writes cached prefixes. do it after rollout across regions. also add TTL of 7d for warmup entries and LRU size bump for 24h.

mike: question: do we want to include system prompt changes in key or treat system prompt as part of canonicalization but separate bucket? some product teams change system prompt frequently and that would invalidates cache.

alex: idea: separate key layers: prefix cache keyed only on user-visible prompt and tokenizer_ver + model; then a small overlay that applies system prompt transformations at generation time. that might get complicated for correctness.

jonathan: maybe simpler: add system_prompt_hash to key but provide a lightweight mapping table so when system prompt is rolled with minor edits we can map new hash -> old hash for X hours (manual mapping via release notes).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: noticed rollout tag runtime/2026-02-19-tokenizer-1.3 queued for canary at 2026-02-19T21:10Z

rina: ops-bot timestamp matches our window. we should capture exact tokenizer diffs. can someone do diff on tokenizer tokenization of typical prefixes?

sam: im running a diff job now on the top 10k prefixes. initial delta: 6.8% of prefixes produce different token ids due to subword splitting changes.

alex: that explains a big chunk. with 6.8% token diffs, theoretical max hit-rate becomes ~86% if nothing else changed, but we saw 64%. so other things (tools fields, whitespace) account for rest.

mike: logging note — add metric prefix_cache_miss_reason label (tokenizer_mismatch | serialized_field_diff | system_prompt_mismatch | other). even coarse categorization will help triage.

jonathan: quick patch suggestions:
- add tokenizer_version into cache key (v=3)
- canonicalize tools field serialization (sort keys, drop empties)
- normalize system whitespace
- add fallback lookup to prev_tokenizer for 4h after deploy
- schedule warmup job for top 5k prefixes per region after canary passes

alex: I'll open a PR with canonicalize + token_version in key. sam can own the warmup pipeline. mike can do metrics and labeling. rina can coordinate messaging to product teams about system prompt churn.

sam: will add warmup job and a flag to limit warmup rps. plan to run at 10 rps per region for first 2 hours then ramp if success.

mike: I'll add the cache_key_mismatch metric and a dashboard with breakdown.

rina: also recommend we add a small unit test to the eval harness that asserts cache key stability when only metadata like request_id or trace_id changes.

alex: thanks — let's aim for a hotfix tonight for canonicalization and key versioning, then warmup + metrics afterwards. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: recorded regression ticket RINF-4123 for prefix cache hit-rate drop. assign to eng-runtime oncall.

jonathan: adding note to run a retrospective after rollout to capture any gaps in release checklist (tokenizer pinned? warmup?).

alex: cool. I'll paste PR link when ready.

sam: ping me when PR merged, I'll kick warmup.

mike: and I'll keep an eye on cost dashboard.

alex: end of thread for now.
